data_description.ota_password: Used once to make a read-only API token for Home Assistant, then forgotten. Home Assistant never stores it.
data_description.restrict_network: The token then works only from these addresses or ranges (up to four). The address Home Assistant used to reach the node is filled in; leave it empty to allow any.

credentials.description: {host} answers. Enter the cluster's OTA password to make an API token for Home Assistant: it reads the status and system areas, and nothing else.

hassio_confirm.description: Set up the MQTT Core cluster the {addon} app belongs to?
hassio_confirm.title: MQTT Core through the Home Assistant app

data_description.ota_password: Used once to make a read-only API token for Home Assistant, then forgotten. Home Assistant never stores it.
data_description.restrict_network: The token then works only from these addresses or ranges (up to four). The address Home Assistant used to reach the node is filled in; leave it empty to allow any.

reauth_confirm.description: The API token for {host} no longer works (revoked, or limited to another address). Enter the OTA password to make a new one.
reauth_confirm.title: Make a new API token

data_description.host: One node of the cluster: its DNS name (as on its certificate), the cluster's name, or an IP address. Home Assistant learns the other members from it.
data_description.port: The node's HTTPS port: 443 unless you moved it.

user.description: Connect to an MQTT Core node's admin API.

data_description.ssl: MQTT Core accepts API tokens over plain HTTP only from the node itself (loopback).
data_description.verify_ssl: Leave on for a certificate from Let's Encrypt. Turn off only for a self-signed certificate.

cluster_unreachable.message: No member of the cluster answered: {error}

node_unreachable.message: The node did not answer, directly or through the cluster: {error}

token_refused.message: The node refused the API token: {error}

token_rejected.message: The node no longer accepts the API token: it was revoked or has expired.

token_cannot_read_firmware.message: The token may not read the firmware's state ({error}). Sign in again to give it the maintenance right (MQTT Core 0.30.0).

token_cannot_maintain.message: The token may not do this ({error}). Sign in again to give it the maintenance right (MQTT Core 0.30.0).

update_not_offered.message: The update server does not offer version {version} to this board: it installs only what its own update server offers.

install_failed.message: The board did not start the install: {error}

maintenance_failed.message: The node refused or did not answer: {error}

entry_not_found.message: No MQTT Core cluster with that config entry.

entry_not_loaded.message: The MQTT Core cluster {title} is not loaded.

token_cannot_change.message: The token may not change this ({error}). Sign in again to give it the access and clients rights.

client_not_connected.message: No node has a client connected as {client_id}.

retained_set_near_full.title: MQTT Core {title}: the retained set is nearly full
retained_set_near_full.description: Raft's retained set fills {used} % of its ceiling ({kib} of {ceiling_kib} KiB, {topics} topics). The ceiling is what the smallest member's storage holds. At the ceiling, a new retained message stays on the node it was published to: a client connected to another node does not get it, nor does Home Assistant after it reconnects there. Fewer or smaller retained messages make room, for example by turning off discovery of entities you do not use. This goes away once the set is under 85 % again.

token_rights.title: MQTT Core {title} needs a new token

confirm.title: Sign in again to MQTT Core {title}
confirm.description: The token Home Assistant uses has less than the integration needs for: {areas}. Sign in again with the OTA password: Home Assistant makes a new token with those rights and keeps no password.

update_rolled_back.title: {node} rolled back an update
update_rolled_back.description: The board {node} did not confirm version {version} after installing it, and went back to {running}. It keeps running {running}; its log (MQTT Core's console, System → Logs) says why the new version did not start. This goes away once a later update succeeds.

add_user.name: Add user
add_user.description: Adds an MQTT user to the cluster. It may connect at once on every node.

name.name: User name
name.description: 1 to 64 bytes: no ':', spaces or control characters, not '#' first.

set_password.name: Set password
set_password.description: Gives an MQTT user a new password. Clients connected as that user are disconnected.

remove_user.name: Remove user
remove_user.description: Removes an MQTT user. Clients connected as that user are disconnected.

get_acl.name: Get ACL
get_acl.description: Returns the ACL in force: its text, its mode and how many rules it has.

set_acl.name: Set ACL
set_acl.description: Replaces the whole ACL with this text. Subscriptions it no longer allows are dropped.

acl.name: ACL
acl.description: One rule per line: allow|deny WHO ACTIONS FILTER; # starts a comment.

list_clients.name: List clients
list_clients.description: Returns the clients connected to every node, with their login, address and node.

kick_client.name: Disconnect client
kick_client.description: Disconnects a client from whichever node it is connected to (MQTT 5: reason 0x98). Its session stays.

init.title: The cluster's listeners
init.description: Listener settings are the cluster's, shared by every node that follows them, and used from each node's next start. Changing them needs the OTA password, which Home Assistant does not keep.

listeners.title: The cluster's listeners
listeners.description: Each server on or off, and its port. No two servers that are on may share a port. {error}

data_description.http_enabled: Plain HTTP may be off only while HTTPS serves with a certificate; its port stays reserved for the fallback.
data_description.ws_path: The path both WebSocket listeners answer on, such as /mqtt.
